title: Verse 1
words: ū kāvyadatiśaya jñāna sāmrājya śrīkara vaybhava bhadrabhūkaravāda bhūvalaya siddhāntakū kāvyadīdiyōḷ namipe

translation: I bow to the Bhūvalaya doctrine, described in terms of extraordinary knowledge, a realm, auspicious splendor, and an unclear phrase about bringing good to the earth. The opening syllable and the phrase before “I bow” remain unclear.

title: Verse 2
words: vaśavālōka alōka bhūvalayada traśanāḷiyōḷa hōragiruva yaśataniyāda jñānada ghana vadanāḷvarasave mangalada prābhrutavu

translation: The line mentions the world and non-world, the inside and outside of the earth-circle’s trasa-nāḍī, and knowledge. Its middle phrase cannot be read securely; it ends by calling something an auspicious offering.

title: Verse 3

title: Verse 4

restored: vāda aidu bhāṣeya śrīnivāsāgama kāvya nayamārga pramāṇada aṃkade barpudāda anēkāṃta ēkavastu dravyava
translation: …which is so, of five languages; the Śrīnivāsa āgama poem’s substance, which, through the method of standpoints, comes forth in the number of the standard—many-sided, a single entity…

title: Verse 266
words: du avināśiyastdravya hti ?adu huṭṭadu ēhi hitavākyagīteya arthāgamadravyatatiśaya vidu satatāś
restored: adu avināśi asti dravya hi adu huṭṭadu eṃba hitavākya gīteya artha āgamadravyada atiśayavidu satata
translation: It is imperishable; substance indeed exists. The beneficial statement that it is not born is the meaning of the Gītā. This is always the extraordinary quality of the substance described in scripture.

title: Verse 266
words: aadakṣaradagītārthadaṣṭāda śasa adina kurukṣētra naḍesi khageyda arthavu hadinenṭaradhyāyararali baruvu
restored: a akṣarada gītārthada aṣṭādaśa dina kurukṣētra naḍesi geyda arthavu hadineṃṭu adhyāyagaḷali baruvu.
translation: Of the Gītā-meaning of the letter a, the import of Kurukṣetra conducted and performed for eighteen days appears in eighteen chapters.

title: Verse 267
translation: Ascertainment.

title: Verse 268
words: nhada kāvydehattu sāviradōmbhaynūr saha mūvattaidarankagaḷuvahisidak?aravadu yuddhānkadōḷu kūḍi mahimeya samsārdanka
restored: mahad kāvyada hattu sāvirada oṃbainūra saha mūvattaidara aṃkagaḷu vahisida akṣaravadu yuddhāṃkadoḷu kūḍi mahimeya saṃsārada aṃka
translation: That letter which the ten thousand nine hundred and thirty-five numerals of the great poem bore, joining within the war-number, is the number of glorious saṃsāra.

title: Verse 269
words: cahādanu antara hadināru sāviram hi nālnūrēḷankaverayi mahāyuddha bharata bhārata gōmaṭk ruṣṇshneyshne bhūvlaym
restored: cahādanu aṃtara hadināru sāviraṃ hi nālnūrēḷ aṃkava eṇeyi mahāyuddha bharata bhārata gōmaṭa kṛṣṇa sahaneya sahane bhūvalayaṃ
translation: He desired; thereafter, count sixteen thousand, indeed four hundred seven numbers. The great war, Bharata, the Bhārata narrative, Gomaṭa, Kṛṣṇa: Bhūvalaya is the forbearance of forbearance.

title: Verse 1
words: ē savva arahantāṇam kāvyadōḷ śrīśarippatnālvar siddharā sarvavarmūvaru gurugaḷōḷādimar śrīśaru vruṣabha bhūvalaya
restored: ē savva arahaṃtāṇaṃ kāvyadoḷ śrīśar ippattanālvar siddhar ā sarvavar mūvaru gurugaḷoḷ ādimar śrīśaru ṛṣabha bhūvalaya
translation: In the poem ‘Ē savva arahaṃtāṇaṃ’, among the twenty-four glorious lords, those Siddhas—all of them—and the three teachers, the foremost glorious lord Ṛṣabha [imparts] Bhūvalaya.

title: Verse 2
words: varadanugrahageydu vruṣabhasēnarigandu bharatanigōredudanindu siri mahḷvīraru guru gavtamarige vara śrēṇikanige pēḷdant
restored: varadānugraha gaidu ṛṣabhasēnarige aṃdu bharatanige oredudanu iṃdu siri mahāvīraru guru gautamarige vara śrēṇikanige pēḷdaṃte
translation: As Śrī Mahāvīra now told the teacher Gautama and the excellent Śreṇika that which Ṛṣabha, having bestowed boon-giving grace, then expounded to Ṛṣabhasena and Bharata.

title: Verse 3
words: mvā hari vara kuruvamśada nēmiya pavitrada karmāṭaruddh? kivigaḷge pra?am?nuyōgadanādiya saviya triṣaṣṭipuruṣari
restored: mahā hari vara kuruvaṃśada nēmiya pavitrada karṇāṭa vṛddha kavigaḷge prathamānuyōgada anādiya saviya triṣaṣṭi puruṣara ī
translation: Of great Hari, of Nemi of the excellent Kuru lineage, of the sacred; to the senior Kannada poets; of Prathamānuyoga, of beginningless sweetness, of the sixty-three persons—this [work].

title: Verse 4
words: karmāṭakavu māgadha mālavagavuḍa gurjara lāḍavu sēri sarvaru kuru hariyaduvamś?darasarge pērmeya guru brāmhaṇ?nka
restored: karmāṭakavū māgadha mālava gauḍa gurjara lāḍavū sēri sarvaru kuru hari yadu vaṃśada arasarge pērmeya guru brāhmaṇāṃka
translation: Karnataka, Māgadha, Mālava, Gauḍa, Gurjara and Lāḍa being included, for all the kings of the Kuru, Hari and Yadu lineages, the honoured teacher bears the designation Brāhmaṇa.

title: Verse 5
words: lthadanka śrēṇḷyanarita drōṇācāryanatiśaya śaradōḷu kabba hitadndrakīla parvatake hattalu pārthanutisida kāvya stutnpāpahara
restored: labdha aṃkaśrēṇiyan arita drōṇācāryana atiśaya śaradoḷu kabba hita; iṃdrakīla parvatake hattalu pārtha nutisida kāvya stutiṃ pāpahara.
translation: In the extraordinary arrow of Droṇācārya, who knew the series of obtained numbers, poetry is beneficial; the poem that Pārtha praised when ascending Mount Indrakīla removes sin through praise.

title: Verse 6
words: lā sāmānya prastāradā ra?avargadīśānka śrīkruṣṇanukti ā śaradandada cakrabandhākṣaradā śarathige pēḷda marmam
restored: ā sāmānya prastārada āryavargada īśāṃka śrīkṛṣṇana ukti ā śarada aṃdada cakrabaṃdhākṣara dāśarathige pēḷda marmaṃ
translation: The īśāṅka of the noble class of that general prastāra, Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s utterance, the cakrabandha letters having the appearance of that arrow: the secret told to Dāśarathi.

title: Verse 7
words: ṇdhdankadandada karaṇānuyōgade uditōdaya bandha vidvadmruduvīguka?inayuddhagaḷigu baruvanka vidura parākrama sunaya
restored: śuddha aṃkada aṃdada karaṇānuyōgade udita udaya baṃdha vidvad mṛduvigū kaṭhina yuddhagaḷigū baruva aṃka vidura parākrama sunaya
translation: In the karaṇānuyoga of the beauty of pure numbers, fruition and bondage are set forth; the numeral comes into use both for the gentle contests of the learned and for hard battles, possessing wisdom, prowess and sound method.

title: Verse 8
words: aaandu kaṭṭida gānḍīva vijñānasavāgi baruvanka riddhi navāgi sarvabhāṣānkavellava kruṣṇanavaiva pārthangitta ōmna
restored: aṃdu kaṭṭida gāṃḍīva vijñānavāgi baruva aṃka ṛddhi navāgi sarvabhāṣāṃkavellava kṛṣṇanē pārthaṃge itta ōṃ.
translation: The numeral coming forth as specialized knowledge of the Gāṇḍīva strung then, supernatural power becoming new—all the numerals of all languages Kṛṣṇa himself gave to Pārtha: Oṃ.

title: Verse 32
words: ṭhānada ṇavakāradōḷḷdi ōmdu ōmānuvakṣaradavayava nirā nitya bramhada kā ava japisuta tān sattunanna sērutiru

translation: Chanting the pair of letters called Oṃ, the one present within the Navakāra of meditation, the body of pure eternal Brahman, having yourself died, keep joining me.

title: Verse 33
words: ṇavṝ jīva avanu niścalamatimramhakava mōhavaḷida jījavanindviririya vyā pārarūhadu nannannavennuva māhātmyadakṣanṇu
restored: navya jīva avanu niścalamati bhrāmaka mōhavaḷida jīvanu iṃdriya vyāpāra iradu nannannu ennuva māhātmyadakṣanu
translation: The renewed soul is he, of unwavering mind, the soul from whom bewildering delusion has departed. Activity of the senses does not exist; he is accomplished in the greatness of saying ‘me’.

title: Verse 34
words: i ara brmhavu ōmde dēhābhimānavilaladar sāḷ nara kayda saada bādheyaḍhḷipa ōmdakṣaradaṇuvāgi ma ahadādi madhravenmayayā

translation: The supreme Brahman is one alone; when identification with the body is absent, having protected the human being, it always removes affliction. Becoming the atom of a single syllable, the great primordial mantra consists of me.

title: Verse 35

translation: Of my number called madhyamānanta, of life that is a compact mass of existence: that which arose within the poem comprising a sequence of padas belonging to the section of excellent ślokas concerning that life.

translation: Of what was brought as received sacred teaching, compassion having become equanimity, [unresolved expression], liberation, poem, of the two goods, the name-syllable, peaceful meditation…

translation: What shall I say when experience of the song’s numbers arises, O great abode of splendour, for the body to bathe at the end in the Gaṅgā of letters of continually renewed bliss.

title: Verse 38

translation: “As wind a ship in water”: the meaning of the śloka beginning “Indriyāṇām”—as wind seized the movement of the ship sailing within the mind, the mind under control.

translation: One who understands that the mind, becoming attached to pleasant objects of the senses, gives bitterness and distress, having entered the refuge of the self within the aged, wasted body, is indeed called Paramātman.

translation: Mukunda, the philosopher who understood the existence of the happiness of souls abiding in complete renunciation, in a state of happiness constituting their entire wealth; next, “even these, attachment.”

title: Verse 65

translation: “If a doer of good deeds always has straightforwardness in which desire for the fruit has disappeared, I shall gladly approve of that,” Hari then said to Pārtha with a smile.

title: Verse 66

translation: Let that essential statement stand. Here, having abandoned desire and understood sweet dharma, with knowledge present and without departing, it became the substance of true renunciation of desire for the fruit.

title: Verse 67

translation: The explanation of dharmas, the meaning of ‘how not’ coming from Pārtha, is sufficient. Destruction of all is a great sin. The essence of this story says, ‘Live in this manner.’

title: Verse 68

translation: At the destruction of people, termed a reckoning of living beings, dispassion must not arise—the Lord's Gītā firmly proclaimed this; beginning with the syllable O is the arrangement of the Dharma-gītā's numerals.

translation: Sound conduct bringing the splendour of victory and bringing happiness is needed; gentleness toward everyone; compassion free from desire; [unrecoverable phrase]; O those afflicted by the passion of rajas.

title: Verse 96

translation: The wealth of instruction belongs to the people of the world. To him who is Kaunteya, Kṛṣṇa himself became steadfast. To abandon desire, you became a remover of passion, O Nara; speech in due order.

title: Verse 97

translation: Entrust the battle, joys and sorrows to me; reveal, sir, the form of the unjust men of the Kuru lineage; display kṣātra, warrior prowess.

translation: With my teaching concerning the self mingled in, with excellent understanding free from the sense of ‘mine,’ by the scriptural method through which attachment to valuable possessions ceases—the war that Nākapati’s son performed.

title: Verse 99

translation: Perform battle. The skill whereby the two accumulations of good and evil deeds come to be experienced, O man, is like the moon’s body, having rays of tender compassion, in stirred water.

title: Verse 261
words: svadikārak? bali aridatṣatunvaya atahananada nirsavimm vākyabhuuhtadarthavu rajadōvaḷu tama sēregamathār
restored: adhikārakke bali hananada nirmala vākyavyūhavu raja tama sēragaṃ
translation: For authority: the pure array of utterances concerning sacrificial killing, when rajas and tamas join.

title: Verse 262
words: ōhikadōḷeraḍarava sarasamarā ayatdehinvma cvuyya satvyōhi adaḍaguvu daritagsaṇiyantu āha samaviṣamānkasgu
restored: aṃkadoḷ eraḍara avasara cvuyyasahi adaḍaguva dari saya samaviṣamāṃka
translation: Within the number, the occasion of the two [unresolved wording], the path in which that is contained [unresolved wording], even and odd numbers.

title: Verse 262
translation: Their essence.

title: Verse 263
words: naipudu tamatytēananajaukata sarvarajgaḷunakūḍalu jaipum bangadu satkarmavanadu manaya upramāmṇō
restored: ippudu tamassu sarva rajagaḷuṃ kūḍalu ippuṃ aṃgada karmavadu naya pramā
translation: Tamas is present; when all the rajas also unite, that bodily karma will be present; standpoint, valid cognition.

title: Verse 264
words: khvaṇavāgade ēkāntadelayasnisamluvasāhmuvāge duṣkarvmavara ñāmasevude bhangavu edeyōḷuvaluvinōḷanumānathavā
restored: kṣaṇavāgade ēkāṃtamu āge duṣkarmavara nāmasēvuga edeluvinoḷ anumāna
translation: Without a moment elapsing, when solitude arises, the servant of the evildoers’ name has doubt within the heart.

title: Verse 265
words: ārādiseyalinacaytad puamāvugarita atasvimaṇiraseya saraōḷu dāyādyavaetādriralembanirannāśediśeyu dharmaraś
restored: diseyali niścayada puṇyarāśiyoḷu dayādyavu irale nāśadiśeyu dharma.
translation: In the course, within the assured accumulation of merit, when compassion and the other qualities are present, the direction toward destruction is dharma.

title: Verse 266
restored: janarītiya balla nīniṃ kurukṣētrada apamānaṃ nagidu sahipude
translation: By you, who know the ways of people, is the humiliation of Kurukṣetra to be endured with a laugh.

title: Verse 267
words: ale pārtha samaku nillade nintu rṭharu akalapiyuva e jayabh?radtaladanka kramadatihasa ilabdhānkada bhalangahhiya trisamdhva
restored: pārtha samaku nillade niṃtu rṭharurada aṃkakramada labdhāṃkada phalaṃ gahhiya trisaṃ
translation: Pārtha, without standing as an equal, having stood [ರ್ಠರುರದ unresolved], of the sequence of numbers, of the obtained number, the result, taken, threefold. The surviving wording does not securely yield a complete connected sentence.

title: Verse 268
words: ykyōga bhangadōḷēḷayyathanaśāśā vrkuguipunmahiya dharmi akava pōrevē anhinnvahisayyadaka hisayya ariyankamakō
restored: yōga bhaṃgadoḷ ēḷu ayya mahiya dharmava poreve ahiṃsāda satya ari aṃka
translation: Among the combinations of yoga, seven, sir; I shall protect the earth’s dharma. Know the true number of nonviolence.

title: Verse 269
words: akaḷeyayya mahimeya matisaynaka amage kurudruḷnaramahamītsakandara svargavāitga āgisuvagānpakagēyara mahanīyarmā
restored: kēḷayya mahimeyaṃ atiśayaṃ mahamīṃdara svargaga vapaka gēyara mahanīya
translation: Hear, sir, the greatness and extraordinary excellence of Mahendra, the heaven-going one, [unresolved: vapaka], worthy of song, O venerable one.

title: Verse 270
translation: In which all the earth exists.

title: Verse 294
words: ndakuruvamśadavara ?ahakāvyarīyatgudirināṣāō āru sāv?r?ada mūranka devahisida muntanmudagīte bhūvalayatruva
restored: kuruvaṃśadavara ahō āru sāvirada mūraṃkade vahisida tadgīte bhūvalaya.
translation: Of those belonging to the Kuru lineage—ah—that song, borne in the number six thousand and three, is Bhūvalaya.

title: Verse 295
words: tanuōtapr?tavidāgihupēśthā aṇnaṣvardādaru śnkanarōtārara kivig?mhā ami apunakātaravellavahr
restored: ōtaprōta svaradādarū śrōtārara kivige amiya punar avellava
translation: Though consisting of interwoven sound, to the hearers’ ears they are nectar again—all those.

title: Verse 296
restored: nalisi lakṣaṇakāra nūtana prakathanava eredaṃ siṃhapīṭhakadoḷ gītākṣara
translation: Giving delight, the author of a treatise on characteristics poured forth a new exposition, the letters of song within the lion throne.

title: Verse 297
words: jagakamalavu nenapige jailātaruta aggatet sāgnadēva mōgagamudre tanuvinōmanam gu agaḷatanuva sādhipathanā
restored: kamalavu uggatēt sāṃga yōgamudre tanu manaṃgū aṃgava sādhipa
translation: The lotus rising, the complete yogic seal accomplishes the constituent for the body and the mind.

title: Verse 298

translation: At the end of the poem, [the remaining wording cannot be translated reliably].

title: Verse 299
words: ahādoḷu banda labdhāntavākahigevatmriyādadarardhabhata sārungadrasamatmamaritaḷvumaṇsuggi kōṣṭakada malataai
restored: doḷu baṃda labdhavāguvadādudara ardhabhaṃgadaṃ suggi kōṣṭakada amala
translation: Of that which came within and is obtained, the half-arrangement, the yield, the purity of the table.

title: Verse 300
words: tmaṣimanḍalada mahāmantrkramḷaya ādu naimi vijayana karuṣṇna amavabhiabhuna amaṇāgaga pratilōma anulōmanoda
restored: ṛṣimaṃḍalada mahāmaṃtramadu nēmi vijayana kṛṣṇaṃge pratilōma anulōma
translation: That is the great mantra of the Ṛṣimaṇḍala, of victorious Nemi, for Kṛṣṇa, in reverse order and forward order.

title: Verse 301
words: tacayarayaṇīyavādanatatvārtha magamvruhāsūtra gamanena bhakada jinavār sarvananīykasanata?ṇriddhyamala śrīṛnōma

translation: Jinavāṇī, pertaining to the understanding of the new āgama and great sūtra fit for recitation, is splendour stainless through ṛddhi.

translation: [Unrecoverable opening] king [unrecoverable continuation], by a bee, son, standpoint [unrecoverable expression], concerning [unrecoverable referent], [possibly an expression referring to poetry].

title: Verse 312
words: vaṭḍhadanga jjñānadōḷ nayaviīyavanṭakaṇataradani pēḷdadinṭanāgaḷe māsa andyiiḷeyuvudajnaṭa jñānadaḷateyanōki

translation: When he stated the standpoint within six-limbed knowledge, if one measured in months the extent of knowledge…

title: Verse 313
words: yaṭu gaṇitadi saala śabda bramdhātlaūaṭa baḷu mahava dvi agagaṭalavāgihndanu miyaitabdhyānayagavendu saalavdhāñ

translation: In mathematics, all the word-principle has become two-layered; this, in its entirety, is called a meditation-sacrifice.

title: Verse 314

translation: Standing, knowing—is it not direct—[unresolved wording] within both. A complete literal translation cannot be recovered reliably from this reading.

title: Verse 315
words: mavariya nelasalānayagaḷu yērṣlatavadu ygśtri guṇa ātma avāge balavu samḷkhapianavāguta savi āvavanādayuda
restored: ariya nelasalāda nayagaḷu triguṇa avage balavu saha nava savi avanāda
translation: The standpoints that could be established for understanding are threefold; to him belongs strength also; he became fresh sweetness.

title: Verse 319
words: gānare intu sama caturasra spāmāada arii īvayavadō māyanaḷu barpan
restored: kāṇare iṃtu samacaturasra pramāṇada ariya avayavadoḷ māyeyoḷu barpan
translation: Behold: thus, within Hari’s body of symmetrical dimensions, he comes into illusion.

title: Verse 316
translation: All adherents of the various religious traditions, becoming good and becoming stainless.

title: Verse 317
words: tvō barpa avarerellara pōreyutuvdavgvu jihndvudsāūnavu dinadinkatidūrtu gḍhivāguvutsāvaḷidiruvyuti
restored: barpa avarerevu jihndvunavu dinadinakke gḍhivā sāvu aḷidiruva
translation: Coming … day by day … death having ceased. The intervening expressions cannot be recovered securely enough to give a complete literal translation.

title: Verse 318
words: kdvaykunṭha īvudu hiriyatiiyadhaṇidana a āntavadanubhaytsada mōkṣavnāvu ancchṇgḷapaḍevda svātantryēmīdha
restored: vaikuṃṭha īvudu hiriyavāda anubhavada mōkṣavu; nāvu icchipudu svātaṃtryavē.
translation: Vaikuṇṭha is given by liberation belonging to the higher experience; what we desire is freedom itself.

title: Verse 319
words: kāya ōmdaydenṭu mūrōmdumshadtāyahammṇa antarayadāya enṭōmbatnāyētatē malkaydu ōyamdu bhūvalaya sāridansana
restored: oṃdu aidu eṃṭu mūru oṃduṃ traya eṃṭu oṃbattu nālku ōdu bhūvalaya sāridan
translation: One, five, eight, three and one, three, eight, nine, four: read; he proclaimed the Bhūvalaya.
